title: What If You've Been Wrong About Yourself

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们除了用时间换取金钱，还能赚到更多的钱呢？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，一名临床心理学家，自2019年以来，我一直在开发被动和循环收入流。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有一个振奋人心的消息。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One-to-Many program is now open for enrollment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特的“一对多”项目现在开始接受报名了。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships, and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，比如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the program myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己在2022年完成了这个项目，从那以后，我也一直支持两届心理学家走过他们的成长历程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的推广链接加入，你将获得苏菲的额外奖励以及我专属的支持套餐，无需支付额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalized guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 其中包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四次小组核心智囊会、大师班、个性化指导、一份福特南-梅森的礼品，以及限时的一对一教练辅导奖励。

sentences.en: Enrollment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于11月16日星期一晚上10点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 通过简介中链接的我的奖励页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的奖励。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时都在。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along to Inner Work.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎来到“内心工作”。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, a qualified clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，一名合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: Now, this week's main podcast episode is about neurofeedback, and that's with Dr. Madeline Roantree.
sentences.zh: 本周的主打播客节目是关于神经反馈的，嘉宾是玛德琳·罗恩特里博士。

sentences.en: And it kind of got me thinking about the idea that we're unfinished versions of ourselves.
sentences.zh: 这让我开始思考这样一个观点：我们都是未完成版本的自己。

sentences.en: And I, yeah, I'm always striving to think about how we can make changes.
sentences.zh: 我，是的，我一直在努力思考我们如何才能做出改变。

sentences.en: So I think it's not part of the kind of whole Stephen Bartlett kind of optimisation of everything narrative.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这并不属于史蒂芬·巴特利特那种全方位优化的叙事方式。

sentences.en: But actually, if there's things that we recognise that we maybe would welcome being a bit different or feeling a bit different about,
sentences.zh: 但实际上，如果我们发现有些事情我们可能希望有所不同，或者感觉有些不同，

sentences.en: then that can be really useful as a, even just as a starting point.
sentences.zh: 那么这作为一个起点，哪怕仅仅是作为一个起点，也会非常有用。

sentences.en: And I think when we're beginning to think about accessing therapy, then it's those things, you know, what would be your goals?
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，当我们开始考虑接受治疗时，就是这些问题，你知道，你的目标是什么？

sentences.en: What would you change about yourself?
sentences.zh: 你会改变自己的什么？

sentences.en: And I guess some of the kind of trickier ethics of neurofeedback are, you know,
sentences.zh: 我想神经反馈中一些比较棘手的伦理问题是，你知道的，

sentences.en: is it OK that we are thinking about changing other people, you know, changing our children, changing the way that they are?
sentences.zh: 我们考虑改变其他人，比如改变我们的孩子，改变他们的现状，这可以吗？

sentences.en: And there's been some kind of ethical discussion around that that I seem to remember when I read Seaburn Fisher's book and the book by Bessel van der Kolk as well.
sentences.zh: 围绕这一点有一些伦理讨论，我记得当我阅读西本·费雪的书以及巴塞尔·范德科克的书时看到过。

sentences.en: But yeah, you know, not being finished, it's that idea that our brain has always got this ability to learn.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，你知道，没有完成，就是那种我们的的大脑永远具备学习能力的观点。

sentences.en: Our habits can change.
sentences.zh: 我们的习惯可以改变。

sentences.en: Our, you know, relational patterns can change.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们的关系模式可以改变。

sentences.en: We don't necessarily need to accept the status quo of how it is right now.
sentences.zh: 我们不一定需要接受现状，也就是目前这种状态。

sentences.en: And I think that's different than saying that you are broken or that someone else is broken.
sentences.zh: 我认为这与说你坏掉了或者别人坏掉了是不同的。

sentences.en: It's having that belief in the ability to change, to adapt, to, I guess, as Madeline was saying, to find that balance,
sentences.zh: 这是对改变和适应的能力抱有信念，我想，正如玛德琳所说，去找到那种平衡，

sentences.en: to come back to, I guess, a better frequency for you where you resonate differently with less trauma, I think, in more of an adaptive way.
sentences.zh: 回到一个更适合你的频率，在那里你以一种更具适应性的方式、带着更少的创伤产生不同的共鸣。

sentences.en: And you might well have written yourself off for things or thought there's nothing I can do about that.
sentences.zh: 你可能已经对自己不抱希望了，或者觉得对此无能为力。

sentences.en: I know a few weeks ago I spoke about wanting to book a pelvic physio women's health assessment.
sentences.zh: 我知道几周前我曾谈到想预约一次骨盆理疗女性健康评估。

sentences.en: I am delighted to report that I have taken action and I'm already seeing changes from some of the recommendations and the physio exercises that the physio gave me.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴地向大家汇报，我已经采取了行动，而且理疗师给我的建议和理疗练习已经让我看到了变化。

sentences.en: If you'd like to learn more about that, drop me a comment and I will maybe think about making a video about what all of that involved.
sentences.zh: 如果你想了解更多信息，请给我留言，我可能会考虑做一个关于这一切涉及内容的视频。

sentences.en: I think that came about for me because I kind of wasn't prepared to just have that this is me moment, really, from, you know, the greatest showman.
sentences.zh: 我想我之所以有这个想法，是因为我不太愿意仅仅发出《马戏之王》里那种“这就是我”的感叹，真的。

sentences.en: I was like, this is my opinion of what I am like right now.
sentences.zh: 当时我想：这就是我对目前自己的看法。

sentences.en: But I would welcome the qualified expert opinion on whether this is just something that I need to put up with.
sentences.zh: 但我很乐意听取合格专家的意见，看看这究竟是不是我必须忍受的事情。

sentences.en: So I think, yeah, get curious.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，是的，保持好奇心。

sentences.en: Maybe don't take your own opinion unless you are an expert qualified opinion.
sentences.zh: 也许不要盲目相信自己的看法，除非你是具备专业资质的专家。

sentences.en: Maybe seek other opinions about whether it might be worth exploring things.
sentences.zh: 也许可以征求其他人的意见，看看是否有必要进行探索。

sentences.en: And I guess even if you're scoping things out with people around you, that might be a bit of an echo chamber.
sentences.zh: 我想，即使你是在和周围的人商量，那也可能有点像回音室。

sentences.en: They might also have the same thoughts and feelings as you.
sentences.zh: 他们可能也和你有着相同的想法和感受。

sentences.en: So that's why I think booking a session in with someone who is an expert in that field.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为应该预约一位该领域的专家进行咨询。

sentences.en: So it might be physiotherapy.
sentences.zh: 那可能是物理治疗师。

sentences.en: It might be a counselor.
sentences.zh: 那可能是心理咨询师。

sentences.en: It might be a therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 那可能是治疗师。

sentences.en: It might be a psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 那可能是心理学家。

sentences.en: Someone that has different experiences that you're going to get a more balanced opinion from, I think, can be transformational.
sentences.zh: 拥有不同经验的人能让你获得更平衡的见解，我认为这可能会带来变革。

sentences.en: Because then you get the benefit of feeling validated, of feeling understood.
sentences.zh: 因为这样你会获得被认同、被理解的好处。

sentences.en: And then when you have that, it sort of rallies this inner drive to help you to stay on your track, to make changes.
sentences.zh: 当你拥有了这些，它就会激发你内心的动力，帮助你坚持自己的方向，做出改变。

sentences.en: I would love your thoughts on this.
sentences.zh: 我很想听听你们对这件事的看法。

sentences.en: What behavior or feeling states would you want to change?
sentences.zh: 你想要改变哪些行为或情感状态？

sentences.en: Maybe we'll get a little bit cheeky.
sentences.zh: 我们或许可以开个小玩笑。

sentences.en: Is there anything you'd change about someone else?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么地方是你想改变别人的？

sentences.en: You know, if you could strap on some neurofeedback electrodes and be like, let's get rid of that thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你能戴上神经反馈电极，然后说“让我们摆脱那个东西吧”。

sentences.en: What would it be?
sentences.zh: 那会是什么？

sentences.en: I would love your thoughts.
sentences.zh: 我很想听听你们的想法。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for being a listener, a watcher for inner work.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家收听、收看“内心工作”。

sentences.en: I will look forward to bringing you the next episode, which will be along next week.
sentences.zh: 我很期待为您带来下周播出的下一期节目。

sentences.en: Thank you again.
sentences.zh: 再次感谢。

sentences.en: I'll see you soon.
sentences.zh: 我们回头见。

sentences.en: Take care.
sentences.zh: 保重。
